subject: Request for availability recalculation — intermittent DNS reflector incident (2028-05-03)
messages:
From: CloudTide Ops <ops@cloudtide.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, support@cloudtide.com
Date: Thu, 4 May 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Request to recalculate availability — Intermittent DNS reflector incident (2028-05-03)

Hi Ben / Marissa,

We saw an intermittent DNS reflector behavior originating from our upstream DNS aggregator on 2028-05-03 between ~23:47–23:55 UTC that caused elevated NXDOMAIN and timeouts for a subset of Redwood POPs. Our probe fleet recorded a spike in error rates and resolution latency across three POPs in us-west (detailed in the attached CSV).

Summary:
- Window: 2028-05-03 23:47:12 – 2028-05-03 23:55:08 UTC (~7m56s)
- Impact: brief partial degradation across 3 POPs; our client-side retries mask some errors but overall success rate dropped by ~11% for affected prefixes
- Root cause: erroneous authoritative chain responses from DNS aggregator (we're attaching tower_debug-log.txt)

We believe this qualifies for an exclusion or at minimum a request to recalculate Redwood's availability totals for 2028-05-03. Our maintenance calendar shows an upstream maintenance window labeled "DNS patch roll" from 23:50–23:59 UTC (CloudTide internal maintenance), which we reported late to some peers. We are happy to provide additional proof (ticket ids, engineer handoffs).

Requested next steps:
1) Re-run the availability calculation for May 3 and show the partial-degrade attribution per POP.
2) If Redwood's policy excludes third-party maintenance that was advertised and owned by CloudTide, exclude the 23:50–23:59 span from the chargeable window.
3) If an exclusion is not possible, please propose apportionment and credit calculation so we can reconcile.

Attachments: cloudtide_probe_recording-0503.csv; tower_debug-log.txt

Thanks — we want to resolve quickly and avoid escalation.

— Alex Romero
CloudTide Ops

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 4 May 2028 13:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request to recalculate availability — Intermittent DNS reflector incident (2028-05-03)

Ben / Alex — I pulled our telemetry and attached two artifacts: edge_probe_summary.pdf (high-level charts) and routing-timings.json (per-POP timing slices). Quick notes from our side: 

- Our edge logs show elevated DNS resolution latency beginning at 23:47:08 UTC with the highest error rate between 23:48:30–23:55:00 UTC.
- Only 3 POPs (us-west-1b, us-west-2a, us-west-2c) exceeded the partial-degrade threshold we use for hourly availability—others saw transient retries that did not push them over the threshold.
- We observed that our adaptive routing attempted to reroute during the first 90s but queued a small number of requests due to KV cache priming; that created a secondary delay of ~20–40s for a subset of sessions per POP.

Preliminary apportionment (subject to SLA team's formal calc):
- CloudTide DNS upstream behavior: 60% of the measured impact (based on correlation of DNS error spikes with client failures).
- Redwood routing/failover latency (our side): 40% (the queueing/prioritization behavior increased end-user latency during failover).

I recommend the following:
1) Redwood runs a formal availability recalculation for 2028-05-03 with logs attached.
2) If the SLA model allows, apportion credits at the POP level (not global) and provide a pro-rated credit for the impacted hour.
3) Schedule a short postmortem with CloudTide ops and Redwood SRE to align maintenance notification processes (SUP-4321).

Attachments: edge_probe_summary.pdf; routing-timings.json

— Marissa Cole
Sr. Technical Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: CloudTide Ops <ops@cloudtide.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 May 2028 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Official adjudication — availability recalculation for 2028-05-03 (CloudTide incident)

Hi Alex / team,

Thanks for the evidence and patience while we completed the review. Below is the adjudication and next steps.

What we reviewed:
- CloudTide probe CSV + tower_debug-log.txt (your artifacts)
- Redwood edge telemetry and routing timings (internal attachments)
- Maintenance notice records and whether the upstream maintenance met Redwood's third-party exclusion criteria

Findings:
- There was a measurable partial degradation that lasted 7m56s across the three POPs referenced.
- CloudTide’s upstream maintenance was recorded as starting at 23:50 UTC but we did not find a Redwood-facing maintenance notification that satisfied our SLA exclusion policy (72-hour advance notification or emergency ops-to-ops confirmation). The maintenance was therefore treated as an unplanned third-party behavior for our ledger.

Decision and calculation:
- We will recalculate availability for 2028-05-03 and grant a pro-rated credit covering 35% of the impacted POP-hours for the hour in question. The full calculation is attached (credit_calc-CT-20280503.xlsx) and shows per-POP apportionment. Key rationale: while CloudTide's DNS behavior initiated the incident, Redwood’s routing delay contributed materially; apportionment balances these effects.

What this means for CloudTide:
- Credit issued: pro-rated credit equivalent to 35% of the affected POP-hour cost, applied to your next invoice under deal CT-ENTERPRISE-3421.
- No complete exclusion of the 23:50–23:59 span because Redwood’s exclusion policy requires prior communication; we can revisit exclusion if you can show a documented Redwood-facing maintenance notification or ticket within our accepted channels.

Next steps:
1) We’ll post the formal recalculation to the uptime ledger and create claim ID CT-20280503-01 (linked).
2) I propose a 30-minute alignment call week of May 8 to sync maintenance notification processes and reduce window ambiguity — Marissa will coordinate.
3) If CloudTide can provide a documented ticket or ops-to-ops confirmation for the 23:50 maintenance push within 48 hours, we will re-evaluate and may adjust the credit.

Attachments: credit_calc-CT-20280503.xlsx

Thanks — Kimberly Park
Director, SLA & Trust Operations
kimberly.park@redwood.com
